prompt: A hotel renovated half its rooms. Renovated rooms earn 25% more per night, but their occupancy is 10 points lower. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Renovated rooms earn 25% more per night with occupancy 10 points lower.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: It could be the price, the booking site, room features, room type or the guest mix.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: Renovated rooms may be priced above what many guests will pay.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare revenue per available room for renovated and old rooms.

options.text: Guests react differently to the new rooms.
options.feedback: This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: Whether the renovation pays depends on revenue per available room, which combines rate and occupancy. The hypothesis says how to settle it.

distractor_flaws.M.restates_facts: Renovated rooms earn 25% more per night with occupancy 10 points lower.
distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be the price, the booking site, room features, room type or the guest mix.
distractor_flaws.M.untestable_hypothesis: Guests react differently to the new rooms.
